name: Ube Cream Fizz
manufacturer: the Gray Zone Star Beverages (independent street brand)
description: An unlicensed street brand cream soda using synth-ube flavoring, real coconut cream extract, and a softer carbonation profile that mimics the mouthfeel of a soda float. Made in three production sites in Tier 1-2 residential blocks, distributed by hand-cart and local shop networks.
flavor_profile: Rich, earthy-sweet purple yam character, creamy coconut body, soft bubbles, dessert-adjacent sweetness that stops just short of overwhelming; served cold it tastes like a float
cultural_context: the Gray Zone Star is a point of local pride — everyone in the producing neighborhoods knows someone who works in the production chain. It has no corporate structure, no licensing, no corponation affiliation, which makes it legally precarious and culturally beloved. Attempts by larger brands to buy or replicate it have been publicly rejected twice. It sells out of coolers, not vending machines.
story_hooks: A Vexa talent scout is approaching the Gray Zone Star's primary formulator with a buyout offer — and the community that depends on the brand is divided between the money and the principle.

One of the Gray Zone Star's three production sites is operating in a building that a corponation just acquired for redevelopment — the eviction notice arrives the same week as a record production run.
The synth-ube compound the Gray Zone Star uses comes from a single supplier who has just disappeared, and the next production run is three days away with no replacement source identified.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System
